name: Aurelius & Strand Thermal Overcoat
description:
Aurelius & Strand is a Tier 5 tailor operating from a single atelier on the upper floors of a Spire commercial tower, accepting clients by referral only. Their Thermal Overcoat is a floor-length piece in a double-faced cashmere-wool that falls with the kind of weight that makes movement feel deliberate. The exterior is available in three colors — deep charcoal, ivory, and a midnight blue that is almost but not quite black — and the interior face, which shows at the collar and lapel turn, is a contrasting cream or dove grey. The construction is fully bespoke: the fit is calculated to the individual wearer's measurements and adjusted twice before delivery. Seams are hand-finished. The buttons are milled horn.

Embedded in the chest lining is a passive thermal regulation mesh — not advertised, not explained in any documentation, simply present — that maintains a stable microclimate around the torso across a wide range of external temperatures. The wearer stays comfortable from a heated boardroom to an outdoor arrival platform without visible adjustment. This is a jacket for people who cannot afford to be seen to be cold. In the Spire, discomfort is a form of vulnerability, and Aurelius & Strand charges accordingly for its elimination.
functionality: Passive thermal regulation mesh maintains stable torso temperature across a wide external temperature range without active power draw. No BCI interface. No visible tech.
what_it_says: You have arrived at a level where your coat costs more than most people's annual housing, and nobody in your circle will find that remarkable.
worn_by: anyone for whom the price is not a consideration
story_hooks: Two Spire board members wear Aurelius & Strand coats to the same meeting; the tailor has a strict one-client-per-sector policy, which means one of these coats is a forgery — and a very good one.

The passive thermal mesh in a specific coat is broadcasting a faint signal that its owner hasn't noticed; someone installed a secondary function during the atelier fitting, and Aurelius & Strand insists it wasn't them.

A Tier 3 investigator who spent a year building a financial fraud case against a Spire executive has managed to get inside the atelier as a cleaning contractor; the coat hanging in the workroom has a name tag that changes everything about the case.

physical_description.visual_profile: A floor-length overcoat with architectural precision and quiet luxury. The silhouette is commanding but not ostentatious — structured shoulders that taper slightly at the waist, creating an elongated vertical line that reads as both powerful and composed. The coat moves with deliberate weight, each step audible in the fabric's whisper.
physical_description.fit: Precisely tailored to individual measurements with a second-skin accuracy that avoids both clinginess and excess fabric. Chest and shoulders are fitted; the coat falls straight from the waist to mid-calf or floor length, allowing unrestricted movement while maintaining an impression of control.
physical_description.primary_material: Double-faced cashmere-wool blend — exterior and interior are both noble fibers, creating a garment that feels equally refined from either side. The weight is substantial without heaviness; the drape suggests cost.
physical_description.texture: Supremely smooth with a subtle nap that catches light differently depending on direction of touch. The interior face (visible at collar, lapels, and cuff turn) is marginally softer, with a barely perceptible sheen. No visible texture — this is a fabric that prioritizes refinement.
physical_description.color_scheme: Exterior: deep charcoal, ivory, or midnight blue (so dark it reads almost black in low light). Interior contrast face: cream or dove grey, creating a sophisticated reveal at collar and lapel that hints at considered taste without announcing it.
physical_description.closures: Milled horn buttons — warm to the touch, translucent in certain lights, suggesting organic rather than synthetic origin. Likely a subtle, hidden magnetic system beneath for security and ease.
distinctive_features: Milled horn buttons that age gracefully
Concealed passive thermal regulation mesh in chest lining — invisible technology, no visible vents or indicators
Lapel and collar construction shows interior contrast fabric deliberately, as design intent rather than accident
Floor-length cut suggests both formal capability and everyday armor
No visible branding; identity established through craft quality alone
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1 luxury disguised as Tier 5 counterculture — this is ultrawealthy apparel that refuses to signal wealth loudly. Handmade, bespoke, referral-only pricing. Only those in the know recognize the cost.
physical_description.cultural_context: Corporate elite who've transcended the need for logos. Worn by Spire dwellers, board members, neural-augmented negotiators, anyone for whom showing discomfort is a strategic weakness. It communicates mastery of one's environment through silence.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when first delivered; ages into a broken-in patina with wear. Seams remain immaculate. Buttons develop subtle shine from handling. The coat becomes more beautiful with time, never shabby.
